In [[differential geometry]], an '''almost symplectic structure''' on a [[differentiable manifold]] <math>M</math> is a [[non-degenerate]] [[Differential form|two-form]] <math>\omega</math> on <math>M</math>. If, in addition, <math>\omega</math> is [[Closed differential form|closed]], then it is a [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic structure]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Lectures on Symplectic Geometry|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-45330-7|journal=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|date=2008|issn=0075-8434|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45330-7|language=en|first=Ana Cannas|last=da Silva|author-link=Ana Cannas da Silva|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Ramanan|first=S.|isbn=0-8218-3702-8|location=Providence, RI|mr=2104612|page=189|publisher=American Mathematical Society|series=[[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]]|title=Global calculus|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1INoRKtgndcC&pg=PA189|volume=65|year=2005}}.</ref>

An almost symplectic manifold is equivalent to an [[G-structure|Sp-structure]]; requiring <math>\omega</math> to be closed is an [[integrability condition]].

== Relation to other geometric structures ==
An almost symplectic manifold is a pair <math>(M, \omega)</math> of a smooth manifold and an almost symplectic structure. The manifold <math>M</math> can be equipped with extra structures, such as a positive-definite bilinear form <math>g</math> (i.e. a [[Riemannian metric]]) or an [[almost complex structure]] <math>J</math>. Furthermore, these extra structures can be required to be compatible with each other, making the quadruple <math>(M, \omega, g, J)</math> into an [[almost Hermitian manifold]].

However, this definition does not assume any further [[Integrability conditions for differential systems|integrability condition]]. With increasing assumptions on integrability, one gets increasingly [[Rigidity (mathematics)|rigid]] (i.e. less [[Generic property|generic]]) geometric structures:

# Almost symplectic manifolds. Can always be extended to an [[Almost Hermitian manifold|almost Hermitian structure]].
# [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic manifolds]]: <math display="inline">\omega</math> closed. Can always be extended to an [[Almost Kähler manifold|almost Kähler]] structure.
# [[Almost complex manifold#Integrable almost complex structures|complex manifolds]]: <math display="inline">J</math> integrable. Can always be extended to an [[Hermitian manifold|Hermitian]] structure.
# [[Kähler manifold|Kähler manifolds]]: <math display="inline">\omega</math> closed and <math display="inline">J</math> integrable.

Note that, for instance, an almost symplectic manifold might be extensible to inequivalent almost Hermitian manifolds, which is why they are different concepts.

The inclusion relations are <math>4 \subset 3 \cap 2</math> and <math>3 \cup 2 \subset 1</math>. All these inclusions are strict, due to the following counterexamples:

* The Kodaira–Thurston 4-manifold is symplectic and complex but not Kähler. Indeed, it is a compact [[nilmanifold]] and its first [[Betti number]] is <math>b_1 = 3</math>, but any compact Kähler manifold must have even odd-Betti numbers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Thurston|first=W. P.|date=1976|title=Shorter Notes: Some Simple Examples of Symplectic Manifolds|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2041749|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=55|issue=2|pages=467–468|doi=10.2307/2041749|issn=0002-9939|url-access=subscription|author-link=William Thurston}}</ref>
* [[Marisa Fernández|Fernández]], Gotay and [[Alfred Gray (mathematician)|Gray]] described a compact 4-manifold which is symplectic but not complex, hence not Kähler.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fernández|first=Marisa|last2=Gotay|first2=Mark J.|last3=Gray|first3=Alfred|date=1988|title=Compact Parallelizable Four Dimensional Symplectic and Complex Manifolds|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2047114|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=103|issue=4|pages=1209–1212|doi=10.2307/2047114|issn=0002-9939|url-access=subscription|author-link=Marisa Fernández|author-link3=Alfred Gray (mathematician)}}</ref>
* The [[Hopf surface]], and more generally [[Hopf manifold|Hopf manifolds]], are compact complex manifolds but not symplectic, hence not Kähler.
* For a small <math>\epsilon > 0</math>, the 2-form <math>\omega_{\varepsilon}=\sum_{i=1}^n d p_i \wedge d q_i+\varepsilon q_1 d p_2 \wedge d q_2</math> makes <math>\R^{2n}</math> into an almost symplectic manifold that is not symplectic nor complex.

== From almost symplectic to almost Hermitian manifolds ==
Given an almost symplectic manifold <math>(M, \omega)</math>, an almost Hermitian structure <math>(\omega, g, J)</math> can be constructed by means of a [[G-structure on a manifold|structural group reduction]] from <math display="inline">\mathrm{Sp}(2 n, \mathbb{R})</math> to <math display="inline">\mathrm{U}(n)</math> and the [[associated bundle]] construction.

Indeed, the <math display="inline">\omega</math>-symplectic frame bundle <math display="inline">P_{\mathrm{Sp}} \rightarrow M</math> has structure group <math display="inline">\operatorname{Sp}(2 n, \mathbb{R})</math>. The subgroup <math display="inline">\mathrm{U}(n)=\operatorname{Sp}(2 n, \mathbb{R}) \cap \mathrm{O}(2 n)</math> is the stabilizer of a compatible pair <math display="inline">(J, g)</math>, with <math display="inline">J^2=-I</math> and <math display="inline">g(\cdot, \cdot)= \omega(\cdot, J \cdot)</math>.

The associated bundle<math display="block">
\mathcal{J}_\omega:=P_{\mathrm{Sp}} \times_{\mathrm{Sp}(2 n, \mathbb{R})}(\mathrm{Sp}(2 n, \mathbb{R}) / \mathrm{U}(n)) \rightarrow M,
</math>whose fiber at <math display="inline">x</math> is the set of <math display="inline">\omega_x</math>-compatible almost complex structures. The homogeneous space <math display="inline">\mathrm{Sp}(2 n, \mathbb{R}) / \mathrm{U}(n)</math> is nonempty and [[Contractible space|contractible]].

A reduction <math display="inline">P_{\mathrm{U}} \subset P_{\mathrm{Sp}}</math> exists if and only if <math display="inline">\mathcal{J}_\omega</math> has a global section. Contractible fiber implies no obstruction classes; a section exists. Its value is a smooth bundle morphism <math display="inline">J: TM \to TM</math> with <math display="inline">J^2=-I</math> and <math display="inline">\omega(\cdot, J \cdot)</math> positive-definite.
